definition: Supervised fine-tuning appears across these six sources mainly as the stage that instills a target reasoning behaviour before or alongside RL. CoSMo trains on reasoning chains restructured by merging redundant segments and splitting logical gaps, budgeted by segment count rather than tokens; ARM and 'How Far Are We from Optimal Reasoning Efficiency?' use SFT-then-RL recipes (Ada-GRPO, REO-RL) to reach a chosen point on the accuracy-vs-token-budget frontier; 'Smaller, Weaker, Yet Better' shows that under a fixed sampling-compute budget, SFT data sampled many times from a smaller weaker model trains stronger reasoners than fewer samples from a larger one; 'From Reasoning Traces to Reusable Modules' argues the SFT-then-RL recipe works because RL decomposes the SFT-trained compound traces into reusable atomic modules; Dualformer instead trains one model with parts of its SFT traces randomly dropped, so it can run in fast, slow or auto mode from a single checkpoint.

evidence.note: CoSMo restructures reasoning chains by merging redundant segments and splitting logical gaps, then trains with RL against a segment-count budget rather than a token budget.
evidence.title: Short Chains, Deep Thoughts: Balancing Reasoning Efficiency and Intra-Segment Capability via Split-Merge Optimization

evidence.note: ARM trains a model to pick among four reasoning formats (Direct Answer, Short CoT, Code, Long CoT) per task using Ada-GRPO, cutting average tokens by about 30% at roughly unchanged accuracy.
evidence.title: ARM: Adaptive Reasoning Model

evidence.note: Defines an empirical accuracy-vs-token-budget frontier for a fixed base reasoning model, measures how far existing efficiency methods fall short of it with a single metric (REG), and proposes REO-RL, an RL objective that targets a handful of token budgets to close most of that gap.
evidence.title: How Far Are We from Optimal Reasoning Efficiency?

evidence.note: Under a fixed sampling-compute budget, synthetic reasoning data generated by sampling many solutions from a smaller, weaker model trains better reasoners than fewer solutions from a larger, stronger one.
evidence.title: Smaller, Weaker, Yet Better: Training LLM Reasoners via Compute-Optimal Sampling

evidence.note: Argues that the SFT-then-RL recipe works because RL decomposes compound reasoning traces into reusable atomic modules, formalises this as a hierarchical latent selection model, and tests it on synthetic string-transformation tasks.
evidence.title: From Reasoning Traces to Reusable Modules: Understanding Compositional Generalization in Language Model Reasoning

evidence.note: Dualformer trains a single Transformer on reasoning traces with parts randomly dropped, producing one model that can be run in a solution-only fast mode, a full-trace slow mode, or an auto mode that picks per problem.
evidence.title: Dualformer: Controllable Fast and Slow Thinking by Learning with Randomized Reasoning Traces

name: supervised fine-tuning
